rows.text: The prior connected-candidate receipt, section 4, said the refresh assembly "drops non-dirty observed rows". Its actual source retains them: it concatenates observed.loc[~observed.code.isin(dirty)] with the revised full histories, i.e. it RETAINS non-dirty observations and REPLACES dirty histories. The prior receipt file is left untouched; this correction is carried forward here.
Capture exit 0 means exactly that the four metadata copies were captured. It is not readiness, not completeness, not freshness and not an acquisition authorization.

The captured legacy checkpoint is recorded as an observed execution record of a June 2026 batch task. Its filename, COMPLETED flag and updated_at are not a daily cursor, and no writer binding was performed. No cursor, target or lag was produced from it.

The guarded legacy jq_download_execution_r1.py was not imported, run, resumed or un-guarded, and the daily data-plane runner was not invoked even in status mode because that path writes current/archive state.

Exactly the four declared metadata paths were read. All four were present and captured on the first and only run; no fifth path was sought, no directory was enumerated, no JSON-internal path was opened, and no parquet or credential file was read.

The capture destination did not exist before this round and was not pre-created for staging; the supplied script created it itself, which also confirms the no-replay overwrite behaviour was not bypassed.
